recentItems.title: Dancing With the Stars' Emma Slater Reacts to Judges' "Stingy" Scores | E! News
recentItems.description:
Emma Slater and partner Jackson Olson's scores weren't exactly B-A-N-A-N-A-S. The 'Dancing With the Stars' pro revealed that she was trying not to focus on the low scores from judges Carrie Ann Inaba, Bruno Tonioli and Derek Hough on the season 35 premiere Sept. 15, especially as the group was giving out lower scores across the board. “Going first, the judges like to give kind of stingy scores, and I totally understand that,” Slater exclusively told E! News' Will Marfuggi after the premiere. “But now we've really got to show the growth and we will absolutely.” Olson and Slater earned the third lowest score of the episode with 15 points, as Harry Shum Jr. and his partner Jenna Johnson came in at the top of the leaderboard with 21 points. Conner Leavitt and his partner Adele Zaikman were ultimately the first couple eliminated, having earned 12 points from the judges. And Olson, a player for the Savannah Bananas who danced a Cha-Cha to the Spice Girls’ “Wannabe,” wasn’t too worried, telling E! News, “I hope that we can up those scores in the following weeks.” Full Story: https://www.eonline.com/news/1436129/dancing-with-the-stars-premiere-emma-slater-reacts-to-low-judges-scores

recentItems.title: Kim Kardashian Awarded Symbolic $1.15 Over 2016 Paris Robbery | E! News
recentItems.description:
Kim Kardashian is closing the chapter on her Paris robbery. ‘The Kardashians’ star was awarded a symbolic €1 (approximately $1.15 U.S.) per her request in a civil case over the 2016 incident, during which she was held at gunpoint as robbers stole over $6 million worth of jewelry from her hotel room. Her longtime friend Simone Harouche—who was staying one floor below Kardashian during the robbery—also received the same amount in damages on Sept. 15, according to the Associated Press. "We are grateful to the French justice system for recognizing us as victims of the terrible events that took place in Paris in 2016," Kardashian and Harouche told E! News in a joint statement. "The experience was deeply traumatic, and its impact has stayed with us." Full Story: https://www.eonline.com/news/1436123/kim-kardashian-awarded-s1-15-over-2016-paris-robbery

recentItems.title: How Nick Reiner's Siblings Played a Role in Death Penalty Decision | E! News
recentItems.description:
Prosecutors will not seek the death penalty for Nick Reiner. Nine months after his parents Rob Reiner and Michele Singer Reiner were stabbed to death at their Brentwood, Calif., home on Dec. 14, Los Angeles County District Attorney Nathan Hochman confirmed the decision to forgo the death penalty was made after consulting with Nick’s family, including brother Jake Reiner, 35, and sister Romy Reiner, 28. “After a careful and thorough review of all these factors, the district attorney’s office will not be seeking the death penalty in this case,” Hochman told reporters outside the courthouse Sept. 15, per NBC News. “That means that the maximum sentence that Mr. Reiner will be looking at is life without the possibility of parole.” Nick, 33, is charged with the murder of his parents, although he pleaded not guilty on two counts of murder with the special circumstance allegations of multiple murders and murder by means of lying in wait. “We did speak with Nick Reiner’s siblings [and] they made their views very clear,” Hochman added. “We took their views into consideration in ultimately deciding not to seek the death penalty.” Full Story: https://www.eonline.com/news/1436118/rob-reiner-murder-how-nick-reiners-siblings-influenced-no-death-penalty
